transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Nicole (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Arjun (Redwood Solutions), Sofia (Hydrangea Head of ML), Gareth (Platform), Priya (Data Privacy), Evan (NLP)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Hydrangea is evaluating Redwood for model quality instrumentation — specifically prompt-set based regression alerts, A/B playback comparisons, and an ops workflow to triage regressions. Key concerns: latency/cost tradeoffs, private deployment vs hosted, audit logs / KMS / SSO. Agreed next step is a 3-day pilot + benchmarks.

Topics: intro, current infra, demo (Console + API + Optimize), A/B playback walkthrough, regression alert config, security Qs, pilot scoping, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Nicole: hey everyone, welcome, thanks for carving out time. i'm nicole from redwood, and with me today is liam and arjun. we'll run through a focused demo — prompt-set regression alerts and A/B playback — and leave time for security and pilot details.
[00:12] Sofia: thanks, yeah excited. we run a lot of customer-facing generation — account summaries and transactional copy — and we need to stop regressions slipping into prod.
[00:22] Liam: great, can you give a quick baseline — what do you run today for monitoring?
[00:27] Gareth: sure. currently we log outputs and run ad-hoc unit tests, and some internal metrics. no unified prompt sets or automated drift. latency is about 120–180ms for our smaller models, but we're considering moving to a mixed fleet — some hosted inference and a private cluster for PII.
[00:43] Nicole: good context. two quick qualification q's — target RPS, and who owns remediation?
[00:49] Evan: aiming for ~200 rps at peak, usually bursty. remediation is split between ML and platform; ML triages quality, platform manages deployment.
[00:57] Arjun: that split is actually perfect for the workflow we'll show — alerts route to ML with a snapshot + the payload, and platform can trigger a rollback.
[01:08] Liam: jumping into the Console — (screen share) — this is the Prompt Sets tab. you can upload a csv of canonical prompts, tag them by intent, and attach expected outputs or heuristics. we'll play a sample prompt set for account_summary.
[01:25] Speaker 1: (background typing)
[01:30] Liam: okay i hit run — the playback engine replays your prompts across two model variants and stores token-level traces. see here, here's the A/B playback view. left column is baseline model, right is candidate. you get per-prompt diffs, a small text diff, plus our delta metrics — BLEU-like, embedding-similarity, and custom metrics.
[01:49] Sofia: real question — how do you surface regressions vs noise? we get false alarms when prompts are paraphrased.
[01:56] Liam: totally. you can configure sensitivity thresholds per-metric and set a rolling baseline window. plus we have a 'semantic bucketing' step — similar prompts are clustered so paraphrases don't explode alerts. for edge cases you can pin specific prompts to be always checked with strict tolerances.
[02:17] Gareth: and where do alerts go? slack? pager?
[02:20] Liam: multiple sinks — webhook, slack, jira, and we also log a snapshot artifact in S3 (or your private bucket) for forensic replay. the alert payload includes inputs, outputs, model, token cost, and the KV cache snapshot reference when available.
[02:36] Nicole: note — KV cache is sometimes transcribed as 'k v cache' in docs, apologies for the noise.
[02:40] Sophia: (laughs) noted.
[02:44] Priya: security question: when you say private bucket or s3, can that be our VPC-only bucket and use our KMS keys? we can't have plaintext outputs leave our network.
[02:53] Nicole: yes — with Redwood Private we can stage artifacts entirely inside your VPC, use your KMS/HSM, and the control plane just references pointers. we also support customer-managed encryption keys and audit logs with retention policies.
[03:08] Priya: what about SSO & RBAC? enterprise needs group-level roles and SCIM.
[03:13] Arjun: we've got SAML/SCIM integrations, granular RBAC at token/model/route level, and audit trails that tie actions to users. SOC2 and ISO certifications details are in the security whitepaper i'll link after.
[03:26] Evan: curious about the A/B playback scale — if we run 10k prompts across two models nightly, how expensive is that?
[03:32] Liam: cost depends on model size and batching. Optimize will suggest batching and quantized variants for playback; you can also run playback on cheaper quantized variants that are compatible. for example, a nightly run of 10k short prompts on a 4-bit quantized candidate can cut token compute by ~60–70% vs full fp16. but we always show the delta in your cost dashboard so you can balance fidelity vs cost.
[03:56] Sofia: good. our priority is fidelity for customer-facing text. we can't accept QA-level drops.
[04:02] Liam: understood — you can configure a 'golden' subset of prompts that always use the highest-fidelity runner; the rest use cheaper variants. playback UI marks which prompts ran on high-fidelity and which on proxy models.
[04:18] Nicole: quick demo of regression alerts config — (screen share) — here's a rule: if semantic-similarity drops below 0.82 AND diversity score increases by 0.15, fire a P1 alert. you can add an automatic canary rollback policy on the route.
[04:33] Gareth: can you show the alert payload?
[04:35] Liam: yep — payload shows prompt id, timestamps, model versions, diffs, metric deltas, sample outputs, and a link to the recorded session (playback token). here's an example link: https://redwood.com/playback/xyz (demo only).
[04:49] Speaker 2: (typing)
[04:54] Sofia: i see a screenshot where you have token-level timing — can we get per-token latency breakdowns? we suspect some tokens spike due to long prompts.
[05:03] Liam: yes, token timing and sub-second latency histogram is available; Console shows p50/p95/p99 at token and response level. that helps separate model compute vs network.
[05:15] Priya: on compliance, what logs are stored? how long? and can retention be set per-customer?
[05:21] Arjun: retention is configurable per-route; exports include audit logs, request/response artifacts (if enabled), and the metadata necessary for reproducing a request. we also support purge APIs for GDPR requests.
[05:35] Nicole: quick interjection — to set expectations, the pilot we're proposing includes: a 3-day playback run to exercise the prompt sets, standard regression rules, and a basic webhook to your Jira for triage. we'll provide the benchmark script and a perf sheet.
[05:49] Gareth: timeline question — we have an upcoming release in early april; can we have pilot results before then?
[05:55] Nicole: yes — if we start the pilot the week of 2026-03-22, we can deliver a performance and regression report by 2026-03-26.
[06:04] Evan: any blockers for us to run this in private? network-wise we have a VPC and strict egress policies.
[06:09] Liam: for Redwood Private we provide an installer that runs in your subnet and connects to the control plane via a customer-initiated outbound-only tunnel. no inbound access required. all artifacts can remain in your VPC, and KMS handles encryption.
[06:23] Sofia: what about model variants? we have a few proprietary fine-tunes — can playback compare candidate variants where one is a fine-tune and one is a base-open model?
[06:33] Liam: yes — Playback is model-agnostic. you pair any two versions the runtime can execute, and the engine aligns tokens for diffing. small caveat: for non-deterministic models we do multiple-sample runs and use aggregated metrics to reduce noise.
[06:49] Priya: do you retain outputs for longer during pilots for debugging? we might need longer retention just for audit during the pilot window.
[06:55] Arjun: sure, retention for pilot artifacts can be extended; we can also stage them to your dedicated bucket for longer-term archive.
[07:04] Nicole: technical deep dive — liam, could you show a short run of A/B playback focusing on a prompt that regressed last quarter in hydrangea?
[07:12] Liam: sure — i'm uploading their sample prompt (sanitized) — running now. (pause) here's the live diff. baseline: 'acct_summary_v1', candidate: 'acct-v2-tuned'. you can see the embedding sim drop from 0.92 to 0.78 and the grammar score decreased. the tool highlights the affected sentences and line-level diffs.
[07:35] Sofia: that exact kind of diff would have prevented an incident — can the playback open a ticket with the model owner automatically?
[07:40] Liam: yes, rule-based routing can open a Jira ticket, assign to a team, and attach the playback artifact. it can also attach a rollback suggestion if the rollback policy is enabled.
[07:51] Gareth: smaller question — how fast is playback? if i trigger a playback for 2k prompts, what's elapsed time approx?
[07:58] Liam: depends on runner sizing and batching. on Dedicated we can parallelize across nodes and finish 2k short prompts in minutes; on hosted it may take longer unless you configure burst capacity. Optimize can recommend runner sizing to meet your desired wall-clock.
[08:12] Sofia: let's talk about false positives — can we add human-in-the-loop gating? we want an ML engineer to sign-off before rollbacks.
[08:20] Liam: that's typical — you can require manual approval in the rollout policy. we also surface a suggested reason and a confidence score, which helps triage.
[08:29] Priya: a policy question — are storage artifacts encrypted at rest with our KMS? we need that for vendor review.
[08:35] Arjun: yes — customer-managed keys are supported and documented. i'll attach the KMS integration doc after the call.
[08:43] Nicole: switching to API — the same regressions and playback run can be triggered via API, here's a snippet (reads): POST /v1/playback with body {prompt_set_id, models: [base, candidate], metrics: [...], sink: 's3'}. response returns a job id for polling.
[09:02] Evan: will the API also return token-level costs so we can attribute cost to prompts?
[09:06] Liam: yes — each run includes per-prompt token usage and an estimated compute cost; the billing export can be mapped to your cost center tags.
[09:13] Sofia: who usually attends pilot reviews? we want the right stake holders.
[09:17] Nicole: typical pilot review includes: ML lead, Platform eng, Security contact, and one stakeholder from product. we'll add they to the invite.
[09:26] Nicole: quick Q — any hard no's on hosted?
[09:29] Gareth: we prefer private for PII workflows; for non-PII staging we may use hosted.
[09:34] Nicole: got it.
[09:36] Liam: security note — for private deployments we maintain the same Console UI via a customer-hosted control plane UI, so ops experience is identical.
[09:46] Priya: data residency — we need artifacts retained in eu region. can that be enforced?
[09:50] Arjun: yes region pinning is supported; retention and region are configurable per-route.
[09:56] Speaker 3: (typing)
[10:02] Sofia: ok let's surface a few edge cases — multi-turn prompts where state matters. how does playback handle KV cache or context that changes across turns?
[10:12] Liam: we support session playback which recreates the KV cache for multi-turn, the artifact includes session state snapshots. for cases where the model is non-deterministic we run N-shot replays and provide aggregated diffs.
[10:25] Gareth: for the 3-day pilot do you recommend we include live traffic capture or only synthetic prompt sets?
[10:31] Nicole: recommend both — synthetic canonical prompts for deterministic checks and a sampled live traffic capture (scrubbed) to detect regressions you won't find in synthetic tests.
[10:40] Evan: scrubbed meaning PII removed automatically?
[10:44] Arjun: we provide a scrubber that can be configured with rules; for total isolation you can run the scrubber inside your network and only share the tokenized + anonymized payloads.
[10:55] Priya: who signs the pilot SOW? we need an NDA addendum for some data.
[10:59] Nicole: we'll attach the NDA addendum to the SOW; our legal can accept your standard addendum or we can propose one.
[11:07] Liam: quick demo note — Optimize will also run a small cost-sensitivity analysis for the candidate vs baseline so you can see tradeoffs if you quantize or batch more aggressively.
[11:19] Sophie: (sic — Sofia) that's useful.
[11:22] Nicole: ok final section — risk & mitigations. common questions are: what if a rollback fails? our platform supports automatic fallback to a safe variant and also alerts Ops. for canary failures we keep traffic on baseline until resolved.
[11:40] Gareth: do you support manual code-level instrumentation for internal metrics? we push custom metrics to Datadog.
[11:46] Arjun: we export metrics to datadog, prometheus, and also provide direct webhooks if you have a custom ingestion.
[11:54] Priya: last compliance question — penetration test reports?
[11:58] Nicole: we can share redacted pentest reports under NDA; i'll coordinate via your security contact.
[12:06] Liam: ok quick recap: pilot scope is 3 days, run prompt-set playback + A/B comparison, wire in a webhook to your Jira for triage, share perf/accuracy report and cost delta.
[12:18] Nicole: next steps recap: nicole send pricing/SOW & nda addendum; liam send benchmark script and perf sheet; hydrangea to provide prompt sets and failure examples. schedule kickoff week of 3/22.
[12:30] Sofia: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:35] Nicole: thanks — we'll follow up with links: security whitepaper (https://redwood.com/security-whitepaper), pilot SOW (link to be sent), demo slides (https://bit.ly/rwd-hydrangea-demo).
[12:47] End of recording.
